t: #2332 The Latest Time to Catch a Bus
o: Buses depart at given times, each carrying up to `capacity` passengers who arrived by departure time, earliest arrivals first. We want the latest arrival time for ourselves that still gets us on some bus, without colliding with another passenger's arrival time. Strategy: sort both arrays, greedily board passengers bus by bus with a pointer, then decide based on whether the last bus had spare room: if yes, aim for its departure time; if no, aim for one minute before the last boarded passenger. Finally step backwards past occupied times.
k: Simulate boarding with two sorted arrays and a passenger pointer.
If the last bus has spare capacity, the best target is buses[-1]; otherwise it is (time of last passenger who boarded) - 1.
Decrement the target while it collides with an existing passenger arrival time.

a.i: Sorting makes boarding deterministic: for each bus in time order, admit waiting passengers with arrival <= departure until capacity. Track whether the final bus ended full and the last passenger admitted. If room remains on the last bus, arriving at its departure time is optimal; else we must displace nobody and arrive just before the last boarded passenger. Adjust for collisions by stepping down through the passenger-time set.
s: Sort buses and passengers; put passenger times in a set for collision checks.
For each bus, board passengers with time <= departure while capacity remains, recording the last boarded time and whether the bus filled.
Target = last boarded passenger time - 1 if the last bus filled, else buses[-1].
While target is in the passenger set, decrement; return target.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def latestTimeCatchTheBus(self, buses, passengers, capacity):
        buses.sort()
        passengers.sort()
        times = set(passengers)
        j, m = 0, len(passengers)
        filled = False
        last_boarded = 0
        for b in buses:
            c = capacity
            while j < m and passengers[j] <= b and c > 0:
                last_boarded = passengers[j]
                j += 1
                c -= 1
            filled = (c == 0)
        ans = last_boarded - 1 if filled else buses[-1]
        while ans in times:
            ans -= 1
        return ans

a.t: O(n log n + m log m) — sorting dominates; the sweep is linear.

w: Test mentally on example 2: last bus fills, last boarded is 19, target 18 is taken, 17 taken, ..., lands on 20? Careful — the correct trace gives 20 because the third bus boards 19 then us at 20; the simulation yields filled=true with lastBoarded=19, then stepping down from 18 skips 13,11,4... landing at 20 only if the initial target logic accounts for spare seat on the final bus — hence always double-check the 'filled' flag refers to the LAST bus specifically (recompute per bus as done above). Pitfalls: unsorted input, arriving exactly at a departure with a full bus, and collision stepping. Follow-up: minimize the rank in line, or multiple days of schedules.
